intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including howler monkeys and toucans.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari. Spot caimans, river turtles, sloths, howler monkeys, and hundreds of exotic bird species in their natural habitat. Accessible only by boat or small plane, this remote Caribbean gem offers an unmatched wildlife immersion experience.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hike and Hot Springs
experiences.description: Trek through lava fields and rainforest trails around the iconic Arenal Volcano in Arenal Volcano National Park. After the hike, unwind in natural geothermal hot springs fed by the volcano's heat. The surrounding area is rich with wildlife including dart frogs, coatis, and exotic birds.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Wildlife and Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and colorful poison dart frogs along lush jungle trails. The park opens onto stunning Pacific beaches where you can relax and snorkel after your wildlife walk.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the most biodiverse places on Earth with a full-day guided trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and possibly even a jaguar track. National Geographic has called this region the most biologically intense place on the planet.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a quick snack from the airport convenience store if needed.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Airport convenience store snack or vending machine upon arrival (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance to save money vs. private taxi. Shared shuttles from SJO airport run approximately $15-25 USD per person depending on destination. Have colones or USD cash ready for tips. Rest well — adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Get familiar with the local area, nearby shops, and the beach landscape. Watch for coastal birds and early wildlife near the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town or village closest to the resort on foot. Visit a local farmers market or pulpería (corner store) to stock up on affordable snacks, fruits, and drinks for the days ahead. Pick up a local SIM card if needed for budget navigation and communication.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual sunset on the beach in front of the resort. Head to a nearby local soda (traditional Costa Rican diner) for your first authentic casado dinner — a budget-friendly staple of rice, beans, protein, salad, and plantains.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary hotel breakfast if available, or grab fresh fruit and bread from a local pulpería (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Local soda near the resort — gallo pinto with eggs (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Traditional casado at a local soda (~$6-9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures. Apply sunscreen and stay hydrated. Exchange some USD to colones at a local bank or ATM for better rates than airport exchange booths.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and nearby coastal trail. Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, scarlet macaws, and shorebirds. Bring binoculars if you have them. Best wildlife viewing is typically at dawn between 6:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge accessible from the resort area. Many coastal regions in Costa Rica have free or low-cost entry to mangrove trails and nature reserves. Hire a local guide for a 2-hour walking tour (~$15-20 USD) for a richer wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and relax. Join a free or low-cost community bonfire or beach gathering if available. Cook simple food or grab street food from a nearby vendor.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto and fresh tropical fruit at a local soda (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the local market — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachside food stall or local soda — grilled fish with rice and beans (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes for trail walks. Bring insect repellent with DEET. Wildlife is most active at dawn and dusk — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining tour through a local operator near the resort area. Many coastal and jungle regions of Costa Rica offer zip-line packages ranging from $35-60 USD per person for multi-line canopy tours. Look for group discounts or book through the hotel for negotiated rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-lining adrenaline rush, cool down with a swim at a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole if accessible from the tour location. Many zip-line operators include short nature hikes as part of the package.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your first adventure day! Head to a local restaurant with outdoor seating for a well-earned dinner. Try arroz con camarones (rice with shrimp) or a traditional Tico meal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or local soda before the tour — eggs, gallo pinto, juice (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch included with some zip-line tour packages, or bring snacks and eat at the tour site (~$0-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range local restaurant — seafood or chicken dish with sides (~$10-14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1-2 days in advance, especially during peak February season. Wear closed-toe shoes, avoid loose jewelry, and tie back long hair. Weight and height restrictions may apply — check with the operator beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby wildlife sanctuary or rescue center. Many centers in Costa Rica charge $15-25 USD admission and provide up-close encounters with sloths, toucans, monkeys, and other rescued animals. This is an ethical and educational wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the sanctuary visit, explore a nearby scenic viewpoint or coastal overlook. Take photographs of the Pacific coastline or jungle canopy. Walk through a local artisan market and browse handmade souvenirs — negotiate prices respectfully.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Prepare a simple self-catered meal using groceries from the local market to save money, or enjoy a budget dinner at a nearby soda.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, granola, and fresh mango from the local market (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Casado at a soda near the wildlife sanctuary (~$6-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice dish from market groceries (~$4-6 USD) or local soda

day_by_day.notes: Choose wildlife sanctuaries that are certified by SINAC (Costa Rica's National System of Conservation Areas) or affiliated with reputable conservation organizations to ensure ethical animal treatment. Avoid facilities that allow riding animals or inappropriate contact.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local beach rental shop (~$10-15 USD/hour) and explore the coastline from the water. Look for marine wildlife including pelicans, sea turtles, and dolphins if in season. Early morning waters are typically calmer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion at a nearby reef or rocky coastal area. Rent gear locally (~$10-15 USD) or join a budget group snorkeling tour (~$25-35 USD) to explore underwater marine life including colorful fish, rays, and coral formations.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach yoga session — many budget hostels and community groups offer free or donation-based yoga on the beach. Afterward, enjoy a smoothie or fresh coconut water from a beachside vendor.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and toast at a beachside café (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) from a beachside food stand (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Local soda — chicken or fish with rice, beans, and salad (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling to protect coral ecosystems. Rent equipment from reputable shops that maintain their gear well. Stay hydrated throughout water activities — the tropical sun is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and exploration day. Sleep in slightly, then take a self-guided nature walk through a local trail or botanical garden. Many coastal areas have free public trails with excellent bird-watching opportunities. Look for toucans, parrots, and hummingbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project if available near the resort. Some farms offer free or low-cost tours and farm-to-table tastings. Learn about Costa Rica's sustainable agriculture practices and sample tropical fruits like starfruit, rambutan, and guanábana.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at a local restaurant to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Try traditional Costa Rican cuisine like olla de carne (beef stew) or sopa negra (black bean soup).

meals.breakfast: Pinto gallo with natilla (sour cream) and fresh juice at the hotel or local soda (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Farm tasting or local market food — tropical fruits and local snacks (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Sit-down local restaurant — traditional stew or soup with bread and dessert (~$12-16 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do laundry, recharge electronics, update travel journals, and plan the remaining days of the trip. Check weather forecasts for the upcoming week and adjust plans accordingly. February is generally dry season but afternoon showers can still occur.

day_by_day.morning: Book a guided mangrove kayaking or boat tour through a local estuary or river delta near the resort. These tours typically cost $25-45 USD and offer incredible wildlife sightings including crocodiles, herons, kingfishers, and monkeys along the riverbanks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the river tour, visit a nearby waterfall accessible by a short hike. Many waterfalls in Costa Rica have free or minimal entry fees ($2-5 USD). Swim in the natural pool at the base of the falls for a refreshing afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a quiet evening on the beach. Watch for bioluminescent plankton in the water after dark — a magical natural phenomenon sometimes visible on dark, calm nights in Costa Rica's coastal areas.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the tour — gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from the hotel or market — sandwiches and fruit (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — grilled catch of the day with coconut rice (~$9-13 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes or sandals with straps for the waterfall hike — trails can be slippery near water. Bring a dry bag for electronics during the kayaking tour. Crocodile sightings are common in mangrove areas — stay in the kayak and maintain safe distances.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget bus or shared shuttle to a nearby national park or protected area for a full-day eco-adventure. Costa Rica's national parks charge $18 USD entry for international visitors. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) for the best wildlife and cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park trails. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, agoutis, and diverse bird species. Many parks have well-marked self-guided trails ranging from 1-8 km in length. Bring plenty of water and trail snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shared shuttle or local bus. Rest tired legs and enjoy a simple, hearty dinner at a local soda to replenish energy.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the trail — sandwiches, energy bars, bananas, and water (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Local soda — casado with your choice of protein (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the shared shuttle the day before to secure your spot. Download offline maps of the national park trails using AllTrails or Maps.me before leaving the hotel. Wear long pants and closed shoes for jungle trails to protect against insects and thorny vegetation.

day_by_day.morning: Morning horseback riding tour through the jungle or along the beach. Local operators typically offer 2-hour rides for $30-50 USD per person. This is a unique way to explore the landscape and spot wildlife from a different vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local chocolate or coffee plantation tour if available in the region. These educational tours typically cost $15-25 USD and include tastings of locally produced cacao or artisan coffee. Learn about Costa Rica's important role in global coffee and chocolate production.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a group meal at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, using fresh ingredients from the local market. Alternatively, enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby soda with fellow travelers you've met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes or rice porridge at a local café (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Plantation tour tasting or nearby soda lunch (~$5-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered or local soda — rice, beans, and vegetables (~$5-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Horseback riding tours vary widely in quality — choose operators who demonstrate good animal welfare practices. Horses should appear healthy, well-fed, and not overworked. Wear long pants for riding and bring sunscreen. Confirm tour pickup times and locations the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird-watching walk with a local birding guide (~$20-30 USD for 2-3 hours). Costa Rica is one of the world's top birding destinations with over 900 species. February is an excellent month for birding as many migratory species are present alongside resident birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that is less frequented by tourists for a peaceful afternoon of swimming, sunbathing, and relaxation. Collect shells, read a book, and soak in the natural beauty of Costa Rica's Pacific coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event, live music performance, or community gathering in the nearest town. Many Costa Rican towns host weekly events, markets, or fútbol (soccer) matches that offer authentic local cultural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Pre-birding light breakfast — granola bar and coffee (~$2-4 USD)
meals.lunch: Post-birding brunch at a local café — omelette, toast, and fresh juice (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food or local market dinner — empanadas, rice bowls, or grilled corn (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring your binoculars and a bird identification app (eBird or Merlin Bird ID by Cornell Lab are free and excellent). Keep noise levels low during the birding walk and wear neutral-colored clothing to avoid startling birds. Confirm guide meeting point the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Final full adventure day — book a white-water rafting or river tubing excursion on a nearby river. Budget rafting tours start around $45-65 USD per person and include equipment, guide, and sometimes lunch. This is a thrilling way to experience Costa Rica's rivers and jungle scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the rafting experience, visit a local hot spring or natural thermal pool if accessible in the region. Some natural hot springs are free or very low cost compared to resort-style facilities. Soak tired muscles and enjoy the volcanic thermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Treat yourself within budget — try a local specialty you haven't yet sampled, such as chifrijo (rice, beans, pork, and pico de gallo) or tres leches cake for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Hearty pre-rafting breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, toast, and coffee (~$6-8 USD)
meals.lunch: Included with rafting tour or riverside picnic (~$0-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Best local restaurant — full Tico meal with dessert and fresh juice (~$12-18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting difficulty levels vary — choose Class II-III rapids for a fun but manageable experience for most fitness levels. All safety equipment is provided. Secure loose items before entering the raft. Book this tour 2-3 days in advance to guarantee availability.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beach. Take photographs, collect any last mementos, and reflect on your Costa Rica adventure. Pack all belongings carefully and check the room for any left items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your flight time, use remaining hours to do last-minute souvenir shopping at a local market — look for handmade crafts, local coffee, artisan chocolate, or natural beauty products as affordable gifts. Head to the airport via pre-booked shared shuttle.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of eco-adventures, wildlife encounters, and zip-lining thrills. Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport with at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at the hotel or local soda (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or grab food from a local café before departure (~$8-12 USD)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and check-in online 24 hours before departure. Keep $29 USD in cash for the Costa Rica airport departure tax if not already included in your airline ticket (most modern tickets include this). Leave a positive review for your favorite local guides and restaurants to support small businesses. Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or late-night bite at the resort's bar/lounge upon arrival if available

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late-night arrival. Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access. Exchange some currency (colones) at the airport for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort restaurant. Take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to orient yourself and soak in the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort. Visit a nearby beach or town center, browse local sodas (small Costa Rican eateries) and shops. Rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort for a gentle intro to the Pacific waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on the beach, followed by a welcome dinner at the resort restaurant. Enjoy fresh ceviche and grilled fish while planning the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – included or approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Local soda near the resort – gallo pinto, casado, or fresh fruit plate – approx. $6–10 USD
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – fresh seafood platter and tropical cocktails – approx. $20–30 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and pick up any supplies you need from a local convenience store or supermarket. Confirm upcoming tour bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio Wildlife and Beach Day – Begin your certified naturalist-guided tour of Manuel Antonio National Park starting at 7:00 AM (the earlier the better for wildlife sightings). Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas along the jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into the park's pristine beaches. Swim at Playa Manuel Antonio, snorkel in the calm cove, or relax on the white sand. Your naturalist guide will point out additional wildlife along the coastal trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out to a nearby restaurant in the Manuel Antonio village strip for dinner with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort or a grab-and-go option before the tour – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or beachside restaurant within the park area – typical casado or sandwich – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant (Manuel Antonio) – known for seafood and sunset views – approx. $20–35 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Manuel Antonio guided tour in advance. Bring biodegradable sunscreen, insect repellent, water shoes, and plenty of water. The park has a daily visitor cap so early arrival is essential. Tip your naturalist guide (approx. $10–15 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private shuttle or shared shuttle toward the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region (approx. 3–4 hour drive from Manuel Antonio area). Enjoy the scenic coastal drive through lush jungle roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Puerto Jiménez, the gateway town to Corcovado. Check into a mid-range eco-lodge for the night. Explore the small town, visit the local market, and meet your guide for a briefing on tomorrow's Corcovado trek.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local restaurant in Puerto Jiménez. Enjoy fresh catch of the day and local dishes. Early bedtime to prepare for the full-day Corcovado trek tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside soda during the drive – rice, beans, chicken, and fresh juice – approx. $6–10 USD
meals.dinner: Restaurante Carolina or similar local spot in Puerto Jiménez – approx. $12–20 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day. Pack a daypack with essentials for the next two nights. Confirm your Corcovado guided trek for the next morning. The Osa Peninsula is remote – ATMs are limited so bring enough cash.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek – Depart at 5:30–6:00 AM by boat to the Sirena or La Leona ranger station. Begin your full-day guided trek through one of the most biodiverse places on Earth. Spot tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, poison dart frogs, and possibly a jaguar footprint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deep into the jungle trails with your expert guide. Swim in a jungle river to cool off. Enjoy a packed lunch at a ranger station surrounded by primary rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to Puerto Jiménez by late afternoon. Shower, rest, and enjoy a celebratory dinner reflecting on an extraordinary day in the wild.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or eco-lodge breakfast before 5:30 AM departure – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or eco-lodge – included in tour or approx. $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Puerto Jiménez – grilled fish, patacones, and local beer – approx. $12–20 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear long sleeves, sturdy hiking boots, and bring lots of water (3+ liters). Apply insect repellent generously. This is a physically demanding day – pace yourself. Corcovado requires advance permits and a licensed guide. Photography opportunities are extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Puerto Jiménez. Optional dolphin-watching boat tour in the Golfo Dulce or kayaking in the mangroves near town. Spot bottlenose dolphins, sea turtles, and shorebirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart by shuttle or domestic flight back toward the Central Pacific / San José area, then connect onward toward Arenal (approx. 4–5 hours total travel or 1-hour flight + 2-hour drive). Check into a mid-range lodge near La Fortuna / Arenal.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in La Fortuna. Stroll through the charming town center, browse local shops, and enjoy dinner at a local restaurant with views of Arenal Volcano.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast before departure – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch during transit – soda or roadside restaurant – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Don Rufino Restaurant (La Fortuna) – upscale-casual Costa Rican cuisine – approx. $18–28 USD

day_by_day.notes: Consider a 30-minute domestic flight from Puerto Jiménez to San José (Nature Air or SANSA) to save significant travel time, then a shuttle to La Fortuna. Book this in advance. La Fortuna is a very tourist-friendly town with plenty of mid-range options.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hike – Begin an early morning guided trek through lava fields and rainforest trails around iconic Arenal Volcano in Arenal Volcano National Park. Walk along hardened 1968 lava flows and observe the volcano's dramatic silhouette. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, and coatis along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, head to one of the famous Arenal hot springs (Tabacón, Baldi, or Eco Termales for a more intimate experience). Soak in the natural thermal pools surrounded by lush jungle – the perfect muscle recovery after the trek.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at the hot springs resort restaurant or return to La Fortuna for dinner. Watch for the volcano glowing against the night sky if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before the early hike – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hot springs complex or a nearby soda – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Lava Lounge Restaurant (La Fortuna) – casual international and Costa Rican menu – approx. $15–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arenal hike with a certified guide for safety and better wildlife spotting. Eco Termales hot springs is a quieter, more intimate option compared to larger resorts – book in advance as they limit visitors. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning in La Fortuna for optional activities: white-water rafting on the Balsa or Toro River (Class II–IV), stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal, or a visit to La Fortuna Waterfall (a stunning 70-meter cascade with a short but steep hike down).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart La Fortuna toward Monteverde via the scenic Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer across Lake Arenal (approx. 3 hours total, much more scenic than driving). Arrive in Monteverde / Santa Elena and check into a mid-range cloud forest lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Santa Elena village. Visit a local café, browse artisan shops, and enjoy a night walk in the cloud forest or a visit to the Bat Jungle or Serpentarium for fascinating nocturnal wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a soda in La Fortuna before departure or during the Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant (Santa Elena) – popular local spot with great casados and vegetarian options – approx. $12–20 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer is a fun and iconic Costa Rica experience. Book it through your lodge or a local operator. Roads in Monteverde are notoriously bumpy and unpaved – this is normal. Bring a light jacket as Monteverde is cooler and misty.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Experience multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and hanging bridges with breathtaking views above the forest canopy. This is a bucket-list adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided walk through the mystical cloud forest. Spot resplendent quetzals (February is peak season!), emerald toucanets, howler monkeys, and rare orchids with your naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Santa Elena for a well-earned dinner. Enjoy local craft beer and traditional Costa Rican food. Reflect on an incredible day of adventure and wildlife.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before the zip-line tour – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Restaurant at the zip-line or cloud forest reserve – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant (Santa Elena) – unique dining inside a fig tree – approx. $15–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line canopy tour and cloud forest guided walk in advance. February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal (breeding season). Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light rain jacket. The cloud forest is often misty – embrace it!

day_by_day.morning: Optional morning activity in Monteverde: visit the Curi-Cancha Reserve (a quieter alternative to the main reserve with excellent quetzal sightings), try a coffee or chocolate tour at a local farm, or take a hanging bridges walk through the forest canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde toward the Caribbean coast for Tortuguero. This is a long travel day (approx. 5–6 hours via shuttle and boat). Travel through San José or Siquirres, then take a scenic jungle boat ride through canals to reach Tortuguero. Check into a mid-range jungle lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tortuguero village (car-free, only accessible by boat or plane). Explore the small village on foot, enjoy the laid-back Caribbean vibe, and have dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before early departure – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch during transit – soda or packed lunch – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Miss Junie's Restaurant (Tortuguero) – legendary Caribbean-style rice and beans, fresh fish – approx. $12–18 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip. Depart Monteverde by 7:00–8:00 AM to arrive in Tortuguero before dark. Book your shuttle + boat transfer package in advance. Bring insect repellent – Tortuguero is humid and buggy. The boat ride through the jungle canals is magical.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – Glide through the jungle waterways on an early morning guided boat safari (6:00–8:00 AM is best for wildlife). Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, great green macaws, manatees, monkeys, and a stunning variety of herons and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero village on foot. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the park's famous green sea turtle nesting programs. Take a kayak or canoe through smaller canals for a more intimate wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Optional night turtle walk on the beach (February is not peak nesting season but occasional sightings are possible – check with your lodge). Enjoy a Caribbean-style dinner at the lodge or village restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast (early, before the boat safari) – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Lodge restaurant or village soda – Caribbean rice and beans with chicken or fish – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant – fresh Caribbean cuisine with tropical fruit dessert – approx. $15–22 USD

day_by_day.notes: The early morning boat safari is the highlight of Tortuguero – do not miss it. Book with your lodge guide or a local operator. February is the dry season on the Caribbean coast, so conditions should be favorable. Bring binoculars for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero – optional sunrise walk along the black sand beach or one last kayak through the canals. Pack up and depart by boat + shuttle back toward San José (approx. 3–4 hours). Check into a comfortable mid-range hotel near the airport or in San José's Escazú neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore San José or the Escazú/Santa Ana upscale neighborhood. Visit the Mercado Central for local crafts and souvenirs, or the Jade Museum or Gold Museum for a cultural experience. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon of shopping and sightseeing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of San José's best restaurants. Celebrate an incredible 13-day adventure through Costa Rica with a memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch during transit or at Mercado Central – traditional Costa Rican food – approx. $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Sikwa Restaurant (San José) – upscale indigenous Costa Rican cuisine, unique and memorable – approx. $25–40 USD

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and set an early alarm if needed. Purchase last-minute souvenirs at Mercado Central (best prices in the country). Keep receipts for any duty-free purchases. Pack your bags tonight to minimize morning stress.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Enjoy a relaxed breakfast at the hotel. Depending on your flight time, visit a nearby café or do last-minute souvenir shopping. Head to Juan Santamaría International Airport with plenty of time (arrive 3 hours before international departure).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in, clear security and immigration. Browse duty-free shops for Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and rum. Reflect on an unforgettable 13-day eco-adventure through cloud forests, volcanoes, jungles, and coastlines.
day_by_day.evening: Board your flight home, carrying memories of sloths, macaws, zip-lines, volcanoes, and the pure life – Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or airport café – approx. $10–15 USD
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge – approx. $12–18 USD
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rica charges a departure tax (currently included in most airline tickets – verify yours). Allow extra time at the airport during peak travel periods. Consider shipping heavy souvenirs home to avoid baggage fees. Say goodbye to Pura Vida – until next time!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including howler monkeys and toucans.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari. Spot caimans, river turtles, sloths, howler monkeys, and hundreds of exotic bird species in their natural habitat. Accessible only by boat or small plane, this remote Caribbean gem offers an unmatched wildlife immersion experience.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hike and Hot Springs
experiences.description: Trek through lava fields and rainforest trails around the iconic Arenal Volcano in Arenal Volcano National Park. After the hike, unwind in natural geothermal hot springs fed by the volcano's heat. The surrounding area is rich with wildlife including dart frogs, coatis, and exotic birds.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Wildlife and Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and colorful poison dart frogs along lush jungle trails. The park opens onto stunning Pacific beaches where you can relax and snorkel after your wildlife walk.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the most biodiverse places on Earth with a full-day guided trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and possibly even a jaguar track. National Geographic has called this region the most biologically intense place on the planet.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer with a dedicated driver will meet you at arrivals holding a personalized sign. Enjoy chilled welcome drinks and a light snack basket in the vehicle during the scenic transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter arranged by the resort upon check-in – artisan cheeses, tropical fruits, charcuterie, and a bottle of sparkling wine in your beachfront suite.

day_by_day.notes: Check-in is pre-arranged for late arrival. Resort concierge will be on standby. Unpack, decompress, and enjoy your private balcony overlooking the Pacific. No activities scheduled this evening – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely private breakfast on your beachfront suite terrace. Take a gentle orientation stroll along the resort's private beach, getting your bearings and soaking in the Pacific sunrise. Meet with the resort's dedicated luxury concierge to finalize your itinerary and preferences for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling or paddleboarding session arranged through the resort's water sports center. Explore the coastal marine life in the warm Pacific waters with a certified guide. Alternatively, enjoy a rejuvenating welcome spa treatment at the resort's wellness center – a 90-minute deep-tissue or hot stone massage to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar. Enjoy a curated tasting menu at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Costa Rican-inspired cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and panoramic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Private in-suite breakfast with a full Costa Rican 'Gallo Pinto' spread – rice and beans, fresh tropical fruits, eggs prepared to order, local coffee, and fresh-squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's beach club – ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: multi-course tasting menu featuring local sea bass, hearts of palm salad, plantain-crusted chicken, and a decadent tres leches dessert paired with a curated Costa Rican wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day. Costa Rica is in the GMT-6 time zone. February is dry season on the Pacific coast – expect warm, sunny weather around 28–32°C (82–90°F). Apply reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio Wildlife and Beach Day – Depart by private vehicle to Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 20–30 minutes depending on resort location). Begin a guided morning wildlife trek with a certified bilingual naturalist. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, coatis, and vibrant poison dart frogs along well-maintained jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into the park's pristine beaches – Playa Manuel Antonio and Playa Biesanz. Enjoy a private beachside picnic lunch prepared by the resort. Swim in the crystal-clear waters, snorkel around rocky outcrops, or simply relax under the jungle canopy. Your naturalist guide will continue pointing out wildlife even on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at a premium local restaurant near Manuel Antonio known for its farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine and ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet or à la carte – fresh papaya, pineapple, granola, eggs Benedict, and locally roasted Tarrazú coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic in the national park – artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit skewers, sparkling water, and local snacks prepared by the resort kitchen.
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant (Manuel Antonio) or equivalent premium local establishment – renowned for its seafood, set inside a converted 1954 Fairchild C-123 aircraft fuselage, offering fresh mahi-mahi, lobster, and craft cocktails with jungle views.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – your concierge will have pre-booked entry tickets. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy closed-toe shoes, and bring insect repellent. Binoculars are recommended and can be provided by your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private early-morning birdwatching excursion along the resort's coastal and forested surroundings with a specialist ornithologist guide. Costa Rica is home to over 900 bird species – February is an excellent month to spot toucans, motmots, tanagers, and migrating species. Depart at dawn (approximately 05:30) for the best sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a late breakfast, then spend a relaxed afternoon at the resort's infinity pool overlooking the ocean. Optional: Book a private yoga session on the beach with the resort's in-house wellness instructor, or enjoy a couple's spa treatment featuring locally sourced volcanic mud and tropical botanical ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific coastline. Enjoy champagne, artisan canapés, and fresh ceviche on deck as the sun dips below the horizon. Dolphin and whale sightings are common in these waters during February.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-excursion light breakfast: energy bars, bananas, thermos of local coffee, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Full breakfast upon return – eggs any style, smoked salmon, avocado toast, and tropical smoothies.
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch: grilled lobster tail, Caesar salad, and fresh passion fruit sorbet.
meals.dinner: Onboard canapés and champagne during the sunset cruise, followed by a private romantic beachfront dinner at the resort – candlelit table on the sand, five-course tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: The birdwatching excursion requires an early wake-up – set alarms for 05:00. Bring a light jacket as early mornings can be slightly cool. The catamaran cruise typically lasts 2–3 hours; confirm booking with the concierge the evening prior.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle (or optional scenic helicopter transfer for a premium upgrade) toward the Arenal Volcano region – approximately a 3–4 hour drive through Costa Rica's stunning central highlands. Enjoy the journey through coffee plantations, mountain villages, and lush rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a premium Arenal-area lodge (pre-arranged by concierge – e.g., Nayara Springs or Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort). After settling in, begin the Arenal Volcano Hike – a guided trek through ancient lava fields and primary rainforest trails at the base of the iconic 1,670-meter stratovolcano. Your expert guide will share geological history and point out wildlife including howler monkeys, poison dart frogs, and exotic birds.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the world-famous natural hot springs fed by Arenal Volcano's geothermal energy. Enjoy the therapeutic mineral-rich waters under a canopy of stars. The Tabacón Hot Springs complex offers multiple pools at varying temperatures with swim-up bars and lush tropical gardens.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – full spread with local cheeses, tropical fruits, gallo pinto, and fresh coffee.
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch stop en route at a premium roadside restaurant in Naranjo or Zarcero – traditional Costa Rican casado (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and protein) with fresh fruit juices.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hot springs resort's gourmet restaurant – open-air jungle setting, live marimba music, and a menu of Costa Rican fusion cuisine featuring local river trout, organic vegetables, and artisan desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Pack a separate bag for the overnight Arenal stay. The helicopter transfer option (approximately 45 minutes vs. 3.5-hour drive) offers breathtaking aerial views of the Pacific coast, rainforest, and volcano – highly recommended as a luxury upgrade. Confirm with concierge at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk around Lake Arenal – spot caimans, kingfishers, herons, and Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks) along the lakeshore. Optional: private kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal with stunning volcano backdrop views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – Transfer to the Monteverde region (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Arenal, partly on scenic mountain roads). Soar through the mystical misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. The premium circuit features over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, suspension bridges, and a rappel descent through the forest. Speeds reach up to 80 km/h with breathtaking views of the cloud forest below.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a premium Monteverde cloud forest lodge (e.g., El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens). Enjoy a warm dinner by the fireplace as temperatures in Monteverde are cooler at 1,440 meters elevation.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the Arenal lodge – pancakes, fresh fruit, eggs, local coffee, and freshly baked bread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Monteverde café upon arrival – hearty cloud forest fare including local cheese (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), homemade bread, and hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Celajes Restaurant (Monteverde Lodge) or equivalent premium establishment – creative Costa Rican cuisine with cloud forest herbs, local trout, and artisan cheeses, paired with Costa Rican craft beer or fine wine.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light to medium jacket for Monteverde – temperatures range from 16–24°C (61–75°F) with frequent mist. The zip-line tour has weight restrictions (typically 30–120 kg); confirm with operator. Closed-toe shoes are mandatory for zip-lining.

day_by_day.morning: Guided private walking tour of the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve – one of the most biodiverse ecosystems on the planet. Your expert naturalist guide will help you spot resplendent quetzals (February is an excellent month), three-wattled bellbirds, golden-browed chlorophonias, howler monkeys, and rare orchids. Walk through mystical moss-draped primary forest trails shrouded in clouds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery – explore stunning enclosed gardens where dozens of hummingbird species feed just inches from your face. Afterward, visit a local artisan coffee and chocolate farm for a private tasting tour – learn about sustainable farming practices and sample single-origin chocolates and freshly roasted coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk in the cloud forest with a specialized guide and UV flashlights – spot tree frogs, sleeping birds, insects, and nocturnal mammals. Return to the lodge for a nightcap of warm local rum punch by the fire.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the reserve opens – fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and local coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Morpho's Restaurant in Santa Elena – a Monteverde institution known for its generous casados, fresh-baked empanadas, and smoothies.
meals.dinner: In-lodge private dining experience – chef's table dinner featuring a curated menu of cloud forest-inspired dishes, including locally sourced heart of palm, Monteverde cheese fondue, and slow-braised local beef with root vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve requires advance booking for guided tours – your concierge will have arranged this. Wear waterproof hiking shoes as trails can be muddy. Bring a rain poncho. The resplendent quetzal is most active between 06:00–09:00 – the morning timing is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde by private transfer to the Caribbean coast – a scenic cross-country journey of approximately 4–5 hours passing through San José and the central highlands. Optional stop in San José for a brief visit to the gold museum (Museo del Oro Precolombino) or a gourmet coffee tasting at a specialty roaster in the Barrio Escalante neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tortuguero – accessible only by boat or small aircraft from the Caribbean lowlands. Board a private water taxi or charter a small plane for the final leg to Tortuguero. Check in to a premium jungle lodge (e.g., Aninga Lodge or Tortuguero Lodge). Settle in and take an afternoon boat orientation along the main canal.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night turtle walk on Tortuguero beach (seasonal – February may offer leatherback sea turtle nesting sightings as the season begins). Alternatively, enjoy a guided night boat tour through the canals spotting caimans, nocturnal birds, and tree frogs by spotlight.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: En route lunch stop at a premium restaurant in San José – La Criollita or Sikwa Restaurant for upscale Costa Rican cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Tortuguero lodge's open-air riverside restaurant – Caribbean-influenced cuisine featuring coconut rice and beans, jerk chicken, fresh Caribbean lobster, and plantain desserts with rum sauce.

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Tortuguero is part of the adventure. The boat transfer from Moín (near Puerto Limón) through jungle waterways to Tortuguero village is approximately 1.5–2 hours and is spectacular in itself. Bring insect repellent – Caribbean lowlands have more mosquitoes than the Pacific coast.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – Depart at dawn (06:00) for the best wildlife activity. Glide silently through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a private guided boat safari. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river turtles sunning on logs, green iguanas, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, and an extraordinary array of waterbirds including anhingas, roseate spoonbills, and kingfishers. Howler and spider monkeys swing through the canopy overhead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a late breakfast, then explore Tortuguero village on foot – a colorful, car-free Caribbean community accessible only by boat. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about the groundbreaking turtle conservation work done here. Optional: private kayaking through narrow jungle channels inaccessible to motorized boats.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise along the main Tortuguero canal with champagne and tropical canapés. Watch the jungle light change as the sun sets over the Caribbean lowlands. Return to the lodge for a Caribbean seafood feast.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn snack before the safari. Full Caribbean breakfast upon return – fresh pineapple, coconut bread, scrambled eggs with Caribbean spices, and strong local coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge – Caribbean fish stew, rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, and fresh tropical juice.
meals.dinner: Special lodge dinner: whole grilled Caribbean lobster, pargo (red snapper) in Caribbean sauce, yuca fries, and a decadent rum cake for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The wildlife boat safari is best in the early morning when animals are most active and light is ideal for photography. Bring a good camera with a telephoto lens. The jungle canals are calm and the experience is genuinely magical – one of the highlights of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the Tortuguero beach and forest edge with a specialist guide. The beach and forest transition zone is rich with species. Look for great green macaws (critically endangered), toucans, and migrating North American warblers. Optional: sunrise yoga session on the lodge's riverfront deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero by private boat and vehicle transfer, heading south toward the Osa Peninsula – one of the most remote and biodiverse regions on Earth. This is a longer travel day (approximately 6–7 hours total, with a domestic flight option from San José to Puerto Jiménez highly recommended to save time). Check in to a premium Osa Peninsula lodge (e.g., Lapa Rios Lodge or Bosque del Cabo).
day_by_day.evening: Welcome orientation at the Osa lodge with the resident naturalist team. Enjoy a sunset cocktail on the clifftop terrace overlooking the Golfo Dulce and the Pacific, with the primary rainforest canopy stretching to the horizon in every direction.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route – either at a San José restaurant during transit or an in-flight snack box if taking the domestic flight.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Osa lodge – farm-to-jungle cuisine featuring ingredients grown in the lodge's organic garden, locally caught fish, and exotic tropical fruit desserts, served in an open-air rancho with rainforest sounds as the backdrop.

day_by_day.notes: The domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez (approximately 45 minutes on a small charter plane) is strongly recommended over the 8-hour drive. It also offers spectacular aerial views of the Osa Peninsula's pristine rainforest and coastline. Book through your concierge well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Guided Jungle Trek – Venture deep into one of the most biodiverse places on Earth. Depart early by boat to Corcovado's La Leona or San Pedrillo entrance. Your expert naturalist guide leads a full-day immersive trek through primary old-growth rainforest. Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, all four species of Costa Rican monkeys (howler, spider, white-faced, and squirrel), harpy eagles, scarlet macaws, and an astonishing variety of reptiles, amphibians, and insects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado trek through diverse habitats – from beach forest to riverine jungle to primary rainforest interior. Swim in a pristine jungle river or waterfall pool for a refreshing break. Your guide will prepare a gourmet packed lunch in a spectacular jungle clearing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Osa lodge by boat at dusk. Enjoy a soothing outdoor shower, then relax in a hammock listening to the symphony of the rainforest night. A celebratory dinner marks the culmination of this extraordinary wildlife day.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn breakfast at the lodge – energy-rich foods: eggs, beans, rice, fresh fruit, and strong coffee for the demanding trek ahead.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed jungle lunch prepared by the lodge kitchen – smoked chicken wraps, tropical fruit, energy bars, and plenty of purified water.
meals.dinner: Special celebration dinner at the lodge – whole roasted local chicken, heart of palm salad, plantain gratin, and a decadent chocolate lava cake with locally grown cacao, paired with fine Costa Rican rum cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is a serious jungle environment. Wear long-sleeved lightweight shirts, long pants, and sturdy waterproof hiking boots. Apply strong insect repellent. The guide will carry a first aid kit. This is one of the most extraordinary wildlife experiences available anywhere in the world – be prepared to be overwhelmed by nature.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning recovery at the Osa lodge. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a guided medicinal plant walk through the lodge's private reserve – learn about the healing properties of rainforest plants used by indigenous communities for centuries. Optional: dolphin and whale watching boat tour in the Golfo Dulce (bottlenose and spotted dolphins are frequently seen year-round; humpback whales are possible in February).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer back toward the Pacific coast and begin the journey back to the Aegean Bliss Resort area. Depending on routing, enjoy a scenic drive through the southern Pacific zone. Check back in to the Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the pool or beach. Treat yourself to a final premium spa treatment – perhaps a traditional Mayan-inspired ritual or a volcanic clay body wrap.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail hour at the resort's oceanfront bar. Watch the last Pacific sunset of the trip with a perfectly crafted cocktail in hand. Enjoy a spectacular final dinner at the resort's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast – the works: fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with smoked local fish, Costa Rican cheese board, and the finest single-origin Osa coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or upon arrival back at the Aegean Bliss Resort – light beach club fare: fresh ceviche, grilled shrimp, and a chilled tropical smoothie.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – seven-course chef's tasting menu celebrating the flavors of Costa Rica: ahi tuna tartare, lobster bisque, seared sea bass, filet of local beef, artisan cheese course, and a showstopping dessert platter, paired with a premium wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day, so pace yourself. The dolphin watching tour in the Golfo Dulce is a wonderful, gentle contrast to the intensity of Corcovado. Confirm the exact return transfer logistics with your concierge the evening prior to ensure a smooth journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the resort's private beach – a quiet, reflective moment to absorb the beauty of Costa Rica one last time. Enjoy a luxurious final breakfast at the resort. Pack, check out, and arrange final gift shopping – Costa Rican coffee, artisan chocolate, handmade jewelry, and local artwork make exceptional souvenirs. The resort's concierge can recommend the best local artisan markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) for departure. Depending on flight time, enjoy a final lunch at a premium airport lounge or a nearby San José restaurant. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and luxury in one of the world's most remarkable countries.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a lavish spread celebrating the end of an extraordinary journey. Fresh tropical fruits, pastries, eggs prepared to order, smoked salmon, and the finest Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining or a final meal at Restaurante Nuema or Sikwa in San José – celebrated fine dining establishments showcasing the very best of contemporary Costa Rican cuisine.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at SJO. The airport has a good duty-free selection for last-minute Costa Rican coffee and rum purchases. Your private transfer should be booked to arrive at the airport with comfortable time to spare. Departure tax is typically included in international airfare but confirm with your airline.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
